passage:
At the school fair, students could buy blue tickets to play games. Each game cost one ticket. Winners got stamps, and ten stamps could be changed for a small prize.
Eric spent all his tickets quickly and won only two stamps. His friend Tina played fewer games but chose carefully. She watched each game first and picked the ones she understood.
At the end of the fair, Tina had enough stamps for a prize. Eric had none.
He was disappointed, but Tina shared her prize: a small pack of stickers. She said, "Next time, enjoy the games, but also think before spending tickets."
Eric realized the fair was like pocket money. Having fun is good, but choices still matter.
